note: CommonMark-tree (SPEC.md §5.2) segmentation vectors. This tier is consumed ONLY by the remark adapter's runner (impl/remark-stay), never by run_py.py or the impl/js runner, because the §5.2 cases below deliberately differ from blank-line segmentation. Each vector pins BOTH segmenters and their relationship: `treeBlocks` is the tree adapter's extractBlocks output, `stringBlocks` is the blank-line reference (linter/markstay_lint.py) output, and `relation` is whether they diverge or agree. Block shape mirrors the shared `parse` category.

vectors.name: loose-list-one-block
vectors.note: §5.2 win: the tree binds the marker to the whole loose list (one `list` node, §5.1). The blank-line baseline splits the loose list per item on the internal blank line and binds the marker to only the last item.

vectors.name: blank-line-fence-one-block
vectors.note: §5.2 win: the tree keeps the fenced code block whole (one `code` node) despite the internal blank line, so a single stay reliably identifies the fence. The blank-line baseline splits the fence at the internal blank line into two blocks and binds the marker to only the second half.

vectors.name: marker-in-fence-ignored
vectors.note: Intended divergence (the free correctness win): a marker-shaped comment INSIDE a fence is part of the `code` node's literal value, not a separate `html` node, so the tree correctly does NOT treat it as a marker (the block carries no id). The blank-line baseline raw-scans the text, wrongly detects `stay:x`, and even strips the comment out of the hashed body. This is the raw-scan quirk the string core's Open question tracks; the AST resolves it correctly.

vectors.name: marker-in-inline-code-ignored
vectors.note: Intended divergence (the general form of marker-in-fence): marker-shaped text inside an inline code span is literal, represented as an `inlineCode` child, so the tree correctly does NOT treat it as a marker and leaves it in the body. The blank-line baseline raw-scans the paragraph, wrongly detects `stay:x`, and strips it out of the body. So the §8 parity guarantee holds on the agreeing subset EXCEPT where marker-shaped literal text sits inside code (fenced block or inline span); there the tree is more spec-correct.

vectors.name: blockquote-internal-blank-agrees
vectors.note: Conformance fact, not a §5.2 lift: SPEC.md §5.2 lists loose lists and blank-line fences as the constructs the tree lifts; a blockquote's internal `>`-prefixed line is NOT a blank line (it is non-empty), so the blank-line baseline already keeps the quote as one block. The two segmenters agree here, which confirms §5.2 only ADDS attachment for loose lists and fences.
